data.name: Edge of Space
data.detailed_description:
Suit up as an operative of the Ark Corporation, sent to the farthest reaches of the universe in search of habitable planets to terraform. However, after the long space journey you awaken from cryosleep to find that your ship has gone way off course and is disabled near a strange new world. With no choice but to descend to the surface and figure out how to survive long enough to complete your mission, you step into the escape pod.

Along the way you’ll gather resources to craft armor, weapons, facilities, and vehicles to help you explore the world and conquer its aggressive inhabitants. Your base of operations will evolve from a few basic facilities exposed to the elements into a hardened fortress full of advanced technologies that let you accomplish amazing improvements to your equipment and alter the environment itself.

Be careful, though; almost everything down there wants to kill you, including fierce laser space sharks, artillery-toting polar bears, wickedly quick jetpack penguins, and even crazier horrors. Out on the Edge of Space, you must adapt or you die. Good luck, ArkCo Operative!

Key Features

  • Open World Exploration– Dynamically-generated 2D sandbox set in the deepest recesses of space, explore randomly generated caverns, wormhole anomalies and dive deeper into the planet to discover valuable resources and other rare phenomenon.
  • Crazy Creatures – Hordes of enemies and epic bosses ranging from Artillabears, squid pandas, jetpack space penguins, and laser space sharks; not to mention epic bosses like DJ Penguin and Omegatron
  • Cooperative Exploration – Engrossing gameplay, built from the ground up, to support multiplayer focusing on cooperative exploration and combat with team-based tactics.
  • Advanced Crafting System - Using the power of science, craft advanced technology for weapons, gear and base constructions from basic resources
  • Loads of Armor – Ranging from stat boosting battle armor to quirky vanity costumes, craft armor to survive the changing environmental conditions and specialize in different aspects of mining, exploration, and combat.
  • Weapons – Create a wide-variety of dynamically generated weapons ranging from guided rocket launchers to Experimental Gauss Rifles and discover new advanced weaponry to expand your arsenal.
  • Research System – A new research system allows players more freedom to discover new areas of technology in exploration, combat, base building, and much more.
  • Command Center Management – Establish your central base of operation by creating the ultimate Command Center customized with defensive turrets, hangers and repair drones. Make improvements to protect yourself from the constant environmental changes like radiation storms and other anomalies.
  • PIOS (Power Input Output Systems) – A simple drag and drop tool, letting you design electrical systems as basic as powering a light or as complex as creating your own logic gates.
  • Pets – Create and collect pets that assist you on your epic exploration of space by granting defensive, offensive, or exploration perks.
  • Anomalies - Random world events both dangerous and helpful
  • Vehicles - Craft items from hover boards to massive mechs to safely explore the dangerous world
  • Terraforming - Conquer space by turning the land into a livable habitat
  • Continual Support – Regular post-launch updates will bring fresh new content

reviews.review:
Edge of Space is a two-dimensional science fiction survival sandbox that combines exploration, crafting, combat, and futuristic base construction within a procedurally generated alien world. Developed by Handyman Studios and published by Reverb Triple XP, the game presents an ambitious concept centered on surviving an unfamiliar planet while gradually unlocking advanced technology. Its unusual enemies, extensive crafting possibilities, and imaginative environments create an interesting foundation for an extraterrestrial adventure. Unfortunately, the experience suffers from inconsistent mechanics, repetitive progression, and technical shortcomings that prevent its promising ideas from reaching their full potential.

The story follows an operative working for the Ark Corporation who awakens from cryogenic sleep aboard a malfunctioning spacecraft. After becoming stranded near an unfamiliar planet, the protagonist must descend to its surface and establish the necessary infrastructure for survival. The premise effectively introduces the dangers of exploring an unpredictable alien environment, although storytelling remains secondary to the gameplay. Rather than delivering an elaborate narrative filled with memorable characters and dramatic developments, the game emphasizes resource gathering, technological research, and environmental exploration. This approach suits its sandbox structure but leaves the overall adventure feeling somewhat directionless.

Exploration takes place across procedurally generated landscapes containing underground caverns, valuable minerals, dangerous wildlife, and environmental anomalies. Discovering unfamiliar locations and collecting increasingly rare resources provides the primary motivation for traveling beyond the initial settlement. The alien setting occasionally produces an appealing sense of mystery, particularly when encountering unusual creatures or hazardous regions. However, the exploration loop gradually becomes repetitive because meaningful progression frequently requires extensive mining and resource collection. Movement can also feel cumbersome, while the rewards for discovering new areas do not always justify the effort involved. Consequently, the excitement of exploring an unfamiliar planet is frequently interrupted by tedious gathering activities.

Crafting and technological advancement represent some of the game's strongest conceptual features. Players can manufacture protective armor, futuristic firearms, specialized tools, construction materials, and sophisticated machinery. Research systems provide opportunities to improve equipment and expand available crafting options, creating a progression structure built around technological development. Weapons such as advanced rifles and explosive launchers reinforce the futuristic atmosphere, while customizable equipment encourages experimentation. Unfortunately, the crafting interface and resource requirements sometimes make progression unnecessarily complicated. Important materials can be difficult to locate, and the relationships between research, manufacturing, and equipment upgrades are not always explained clearly. Although the system offers considerable variety, it often sacrifices accessibility and convenience.

Base construction introduces another layer of creativity by allowing players to establish fortified settlements equipped with defensive turrets, electrical devices, and automated machinery. The Power Input Output System is particularly interesting because it enables players to connect technological components and experiment with functional mechanisms. Constructing increasingly sophisticated facilities can provide a satisfying sense of accomplishment, especially for those who enjoy engineering and automation. Environmental hazards also make protective structures important rather than merely decorative. Nevertheless, unintuitive building interactions and inconsistent mechanical feedback frequently undermine the experience. The construction system offers plenty of possibilities, but assembling complex structures can become more frustrating than entertaining.

Combat distinguishes itself through an eccentric collection of enemies that blend science fiction danger with absurd humor. Laser-equipped sharks, armed polar bears, technologically enhanced penguins, and other unusual creatures give the world a recognizable personality. Boss encounters further emphasize the game's unconventional approach to enemy design. Unfortunately, the creativity behind these opponents is not matched by equally satisfying combat mechanics. Attacks and movement can feel unresponsive, enemy behavior lacks consistency, and difficulty balancing occasionally produces frustrating encounters. Upgrading weapons and armor provides some improvement, but battles rarely achieve the precision or excitement expected from a polished action-oriented survival game.

Additional features include cooperative multiplayer, collectible pets, futuristic transportation, and specialized technological equipment. Cooperative play has the potential to make exploration and construction more enjoyable by allowing friends to divide responsibilities and coordinate their activities. Pets and vehicles introduce further opportunities for customization and mobility. However, these systems also illustrate the game's tendency to prioritize feature quantity over mechanical refinement. Many ideas sound appealing individually, yet their integration into the broader gameplay experience is uneven. Multiplayer enjoyment may also depend on finding friends willing to participate, given the game's age and limited active community.

Visually, Edge of Space uses colorful pixel art to establish a distinctive extraterrestrial atmosphere. Its alien environments, exaggerated creatures, and futuristic machinery create an entertaining mixture of danger and comedy. However, visual clutter, stiff animations, and an occasionally confusing interface reduce the presentation's effectiveness. The soundtrack and sound effects provide adequate atmospheric support without being particularly memorable. Technical issues, inconsistent performance, and gameplay bugs further diminish the experience. These problems are especially disappointing because the game's ambitious design suggests considerable potential beneath its rough execution.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, Edge of Space is classified as Playable rather than Verified. This indicates that the game can function on Valve's handheld system but may require additional adjustments or manual interaction. Players should anticipate possible difficulties involving controller configuration, small interface text, and keyboard input. Its handheld experience should therefore not be considered fully optimized, and compatibility does not guarantee consistently smooth performance.

Ultimately, Edge of Space is a survival adventure whose imaginative concepts are considerably stronger than their execution. Its futuristic crafting systems, unconventional enemies, technological construction, and cooperative possibilities demonstrate genuine creativity, but repetitive gameplay, awkward combat, and technical shortcomings diminish its appeal. Dedicated sandbox enthusiasts may appreciate experimenting with its unusual mechanics, yet players expecting a polished and consistently rewarding experience are likely to encounter frustration. The game offers occasional moments of entertainment but never fully realizes its considerable potential. 

Rating: 4/10
